messages.subject: Hierarchical Binomial-Beta model (Using Covariates)
parts:
Hi everybody,

I am trying to implement a Binomial-Beta Hierarchical model, in short, the model is like this:

parameters{ 
  real <lower=0,upper=1>  betab[N];
  real <lower=0,upper=1>  betaw[N];
  real <lower=0>  db[N];
  real <lower=0>  dw[N];
  real <lower=0>  alfas[N];
  real <lower=0>  betas[N];
  real <lower=0>  gammas[N];
  real <lower=0>  deltas[N];
}                                                               // N=number of observations

transformed parameters{
  real <lower=0>  theta[N];
  for (n in 1:N){
    theta[n]=xi[n]*betab[n]+unomenosxi[n]*betaw[n];
  }
}

model{
  for (n in 1:N){

    alfas[n]~.........;
    betas[n]~.........;
    gammas[n]~.........;
    deltas[n]~.........;

    db[n]~exponential(2);
    dw[n]~exponential(2);    
  }
  for(n in 1:N){
    betab[n]~beta(db[n]*exp(alfas[n]+betas[n]*Zi[n]),db[n]);                     // Zi es a covariable (a real number)
    betaw[n]~beta(dw[n]*exp(gammas[n]+deltas[n]*Zi[n]),dw[n]);
  }
  for (n in 1:N){
    Ti[n]~binomial(ni[n],theta[n]);
  }
}

The question is: what is the best "flat" prior or an adequate "flat" prior to the parameters: alfas, betas, gammas, deltas?

Thanks for your answers

David

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Hierarchical Binomial-Beta model (Using Covariates)
parts:
We don't recommend "flat" or "uninformative" or "vague" priors,
but rather tailoring the prior to the scale you expect. If you
would think there was a bug if a value is 100, then you don't want
a prior like normal(0, 1000). We have recommendations in the
regression section of the manual and on a wiki page:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/Prior-Choice-Recommendations

I don't understand the asymmetry here between the two parameters
of the beta distribution:

You can also vectorize this all if everything's defined
as a vector as

betab ~ beta(db .* exp(alfas + betas .* Zi, db);

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Hierarchical Binomial-Beta model (Using Covariates)
parts:
Thank you Bob

The fisrt parameter of the beta distribution is because the mean of the betab is: 

E(betab) = db *exp(alfas+ betas *Zi) / (db + db *exp(alfas + betas *Zi) ) which implies that 

log ( E(betab) / (1 - E(betab)) )= alfas + betas *Zi

in other words, the log odds depende linearly on the covariate Zi.


David
